**1B.8 Research Note: Srettha Thavisin in 2024**

Best-supported reading: Srettha’s 2024 record is de-escalatory, channel-preserving, and institution-oriented. I found no credible evidence of crisis rhetoric that would increase accidental-war risk. The strongest material is Thailand’s response to the Myanmar crisis plus its repeated use of ASEAN, UN, and disarmament forums.

| Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| [ASEAN Foreign Ministers’ Statement on the Escalation of Conflicts in Myanmar](https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/asean-fm-statement-escalation-conflicts-myanmar?menu=5d5bd3dc15e39c306002ab1c&page=5d5bd3cb15e39c306002a9ac) | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | April 18, 2024 | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/asean-fm-statement-escalation-conflicts-myanmar?menu=5d5bd3dc15e39c306002ab1c&page=5d5bd3cb15e39c306002a9ac | Thailand joined ASEAN’s call for immediate restraint, cessation of violence, and humanitarian access in Myanmar. That is the clearest evidence that Srettha’s government favored de-escalation and kept diplomatic channels open during a regional crisis. | `1B.8` |
| [Thailand stresses the importance of upscaling humanitarian assistance along the Thai-Myanmar border at the Human Rights Council](https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/vfm010324-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683c) | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | March 4, 2024 | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/vfm010324-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683c | Thailand said it was concerned about Myanmar, supported humanitarian assistance, and encouraged dialogue, reconciliation, and a peaceful, stable, unified Myanmar. That is strong evidence of clear communication and crisis de-escalation rather than brinkmanship. | `1B.8` |
| [Thailand working ‘relentlessly’ to solve Myanmar crisis - Srettha](https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/2798697/thailand-working-relentlessly-to-solve-myanmar-crisis-srettha) | Bangkok Post, reporting Bloomberg News | May 24, 2024 | https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/2798697/thailand-working-relentlessly-to-solve-myanmar-crisis-srettha | Srettha said Thailand was working to end the Myanmar crisis and reduce spillover violence. This supports a reading of active crisis management aimed at preventing escalation. | `1B.8` |
| [Keynote speech by Prime Minister of Thailand at the 29th Nikkei Forum Future of Asia “Asian Leadership in an Uncertain World”](https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/nikkeiforum-240524?menu=5d5bd3dd15e39c306002ab21&page=5d5bd3dd15e39c306002ab20) | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | May 24, 2024 | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/nikkeiforum-240524?menu=5d5bd3dd15e39c306002ab21&page=5d5bd3dd15e39c306002ab20 | Srettha framed regional leadership in terms of mutual trust, constructive cooperation, and stability in an uncertain world. This is not a crisis transcript, but it is consistent with preserving channels that reduce accidental-war risk. | `1B.8` |
| [Thailand co-chaired the 15th ASEAN Regional Forum Inter-Sessional Meeting on Non-Proliferation and Disarmament in Honolulu, Hawaii](https://mfa.go.th/en/content/arfismonnpd-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683e) | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | May 3, 2024 | https://mfa.go.th/en/content/arfismonnpd-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683e | Thailand used a formal multilateral forum to support transparency, nonproliferation, and the total elimination of nuclear weapons. That is institutional channel-preserving behavior, not destabilizing rhetoric. | `1B.8`, `1B.1`, `1B.4` |

| [Readout of Secretary Raimondo’s Meeting with Thai Prime Minister Srettha Thavisin](https://www.commerce.gov/news/press-releases/2024/03/readout-secretary-raimondos-meeting-thai-prime-minister-srettha) | U.S. Department of Commerce | March 14, 2024 | https://www.commerce.gov/news/press-releases/2024/03/readout-secretary-raimondos-meeting-thai-prime-minister-srettha | The only explicit nuclear reference I found was civil nuclear energy discussed in a clean-energy and sustainability frame. That is peaceful, communicative, and channel-preserving, not crisis-escalatory. | `1B.8`, `1B.2` |

**Search gap**
- I did not find any 2024 source showing Srettha in a nuclear crisis where he had to choose between escalation and de-escalation.
- I did not find evidence of reckless nuclear signaling, breakdown of crisis channels, or messages that would raise accidental-war risk.
- The available record is therefore indirect but consistent: Thailand relied on ASEAN, the UN system, and disarmament forums, while Srettha publicly emphasized dialogue, mutual trust, and reducing spillover violence.
